newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police raid suspected sect - media.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police raid suspected sect - media.

text.p: Police raided up to seven houses on Wednesday in western Belgium belonging to what they said was a religious sect and took their leader in for questioning, Belgian media said.
Television pictures from the small town of Leuze-en-Hainaut and nearby village of Bon-Secours on the French border, showed investigators inside the houses and removing cardboard boxes.
Rooms contained religious artefacts and shelves of what appeared to be medicine bottles.
Behind one house was a large bricked-over yard with a cross and altar. BEL-RTL television said there had been gatherings of up to 200 people there, with some coming from Austria, Germany and France.
The public prosecutor in the nearby town of Tournai in charge of the investigation was not available to confirm the media reports, but was due to give a news conference later on Wednesday.
No arrests had so far been made, though searches were continuing, according to the television.
It said police had wanted to check that the followers of the sect, which called itself "Cor Unum", were not victims of abduction or suffering ill-treatment.
They were also concerned for children living in the group which rejected all traditional medicine and was preventing them from going to school.
The houses were reported to have been occupied by the sect for at least six years, and the raids were prompted by complaints from neighbours.
